quotes.text: Instead of your app holding a secret and proving it belongs, the app becomes the identity. Access gets granted to the identity, not to a shared key that anyone could copy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up in two sentences the shift from shared secrets to resource identities.

quotes.text: So the practical rule is to start with a user assigned identity. Unless you have a specific reason to want the identity to live and die with a single resource.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable default for choosing between system- and user-assigned identities.

quotes.text: Getting a token proves who your app is, but it doesn't decide what the app can do. That's the job of a role assignment, and it's the step beginners skip most often.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates authentication from authorization and names the most common beginner mistake.

quotes.text: If you let someone run code on a resource that has a managed identity, you've effectively handed them everything that identity can reach.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A sharp warning about the escalation path that comes with managed identities.

quotes.text: The one idea worth sharing with you is that the real win is removing the secret, not hiding it better. So there's nothing to leak, nothing to screenshot, and nothing to forget to rotate.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of why managed identities beat storing secrets in a vault or config.

takeaways: A managed identity lets an Azure resource sign in to other services through Microsoft Entra ID without any stored password, key or connection string.
User-assigned identities are the recommended default because they can be shared across resources and cut down the number of role assignments you have to manage.
A token only proves who the app is; it still needs a least-privilege role assignment, and role changes can take hours to apply because tokens are cached.
hook: Hardcoded passwords, API keys and connection strings in config files are one of the most common ways cloud apps leak access. This Simply Explained episode is for Azure developers and admins who want to understand managed identities: how the token flow works, how to grant access to Key Vault and other services, and which pitfalls to avoid.
